les: Die Aarde se pad om die son
kaps_punt: Beweging om die Son: die Aarde beweeg in 'n baan om die Son wat 'n wentelbaan genoem word — die Son is 'n ster in die middel van die Sonnestelsel; die Aarde is een van agt planete in die Sonnestelsel. Die son en lewe: die Aarde kry die regte hoeveelheid lig en hitte van die Son vir die ondersteuning van lewe.

items.bron: NASA Science, Sun Facts (science.nasa.gov/sun/facts): the Sun is a yellow dwarf star and 'our solar system's only star'. CAPS NWT Gr 4-6 (KABV) p. 27, Gr 4 Kwartaal 4 'Die Son': 'die Son is 'n ster' (the prior sub-topic, so 'jy weet reeds' holds).

items.bron: IAU Resolution 5A (24 August 2006), as quoted on Wikipedia 'IAU definition of planet': a planet is a body '(a) in orbit around the Sun'. 'presies dieselfde' refers to the act of moving round the Sun, which is true of all eight. The next sentence says each follows its own path, so it is not read as 'identical orbits'.

items.blok: Die son staan in die middel
items.bron: NASA Science, Sun Facts: the Sun 'is the center of our solar system'. CAPS p. 28: 'die Son is 'n ster in die middel van die Sonnestelsel'. Caveat recorded, not a fault at Grade 4: NASA Space Place 'What Is a Barycenter?' says the solar system's centre of mass ranges from near the Sun's centre to just outside its surface, so the Sun wobbles slightly. 'Heeltyd in die middel' holds at the scale of the planets' orbits.

items.bron: NASA Science, Pluto Facts: Pluto shares the Kuiper Belt with many other icy bodies. NASA Science, Moons: even some asteroids have moons, which shows the range of sizes. Wikipedia 'IAU definition of planet': planets are massive enough to be nearly round.

items.blok: Wat is die Sonnestelsel?
items.bron: IAU Resolution 5A (Wikipedia, 'IAU definition of planet'): in orbit around the Sun, massive enough to take a nearly round (hydrostatic equilibrium) shape. The IAU wording names the Sun; 'om 'n ster' is the broader general usage that also covers planets of other stars, and it is not false. On its own this sentence would also let in Pluto and the Moon, but the next two sentences supply the missing criteria, and the begrip entry carries 'op sy eie'.

items.bewering: Geen ander groot wêreld beweeg op sy eie in 'n planeet se wentelbaan nie.
items.blok: Wat is die Sonnestelsel?
items.bron: IAU Resolution 5A criterion (c), 'has cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit' (Wikipedia, 'IAU definition of planet'). This is a fair Grade 4 rendering. Known dispute recorded: Alan Stern argued Neptune has not cleared its zone because Pluto is there; the majority reply is that Neptune dominates its zone and locks Pluto into a 3:2 resonance. The lesson's wording ('in 'n planeet se wentelbaan', 'op sy eie') does not depend on how that dispute is settled, because Pluto does not travel on Neptune's path.

items.blok: Wat is die Sonnestelsel?
items.bron: NASA Science, Moons: 'Naturally-formed bodies that orbit planets are called moons, or planetary satellites.' IAU Resolution 5A (d) excludes satellites from the dwarf-planet class. Narrowness recorded but not judged false: the same NASA page says dwarf planets (Pluto's Charon) and some asteroids also have moons, so not every moon has a PLANET. The lesson's wording matches NASA's own primary definition, and the claim that matters ('beweeg nie op sy eie om die son nie') is true of every moon.

items.bron: NASA Science, 'Milankovitch (Orbital) Cycles and Their Role in Earth's Climate': Earth's orbital eccentricity changes very slowly, over a cycle of about 100 000 years. From year to year the path is almost the same, so 'byna' is correctly placed.

items.bewering: Daardie pad het 'n naam, en ons noem dit 'n wentelbaan. Die wentelbaan gaan heeltemal om die son en kom weer by dieselfde plek uit.

items.bron: CAPS p. 28: 'die Aarde beweeg in 'n baan om die Son wat 'n wentelbaan genoem word'. NASA, 'What Is an Orbit?' (nasa.gov, grades 5-8, and NASA Space Place): 'a regular, repeating path that one object in space takes around another one'.

items.bewering: Die Aarde beweeg altyd in dieselfde rigting op hierdie pad. Dit beweeg nooit terug nie, en die beweging hou nooit op nie.
items.blok: Die Aarde se wentelbaan
items.bron: Astronomy.com, 'Ask Astro: Why do the planets orbit the Sun counterclockwise?': the planets orbit the Sun counterclockwise seen from above the Sun's north pole. They keep this direction because of how the solar system formed. Retrograde motion is only an apparent backward motion of other planets as seen from Earth; Earth itself never reverses.

items.bewering: Een volle reis om die son neem die Aarde ongeveer een jaar.

items.bron: NASA Science, Earth Facts: 'It takes 365.25 days to complete one trip around the Sun.'

items.bewering: Elke verjaardag wat jy vier, beteken dus nog een reis om die son.
items.blok: Die Aarde se wentelbaan
items.bron: NASA Science, Earth Facts (365.25 days per orbit). Checked as a mapping: a birthday maps to one calendar year, and the calendar (with leap years) is kept in step with one orbit, so the mapping holds. A learner who reasons on from it (age in years = number of trips around the Sun) is led nowhere false.

items.bewering: Die son gee heeltyd lig en hitte af na alle kante toe.
items.blok: Nie te warm en nie te koud nie
items.bron: Indian Institute of Science (wgbis.ces.iisc.ac.in, energy primer): the Sun radiates in all directions and Earth intercepts only about two thousand-millionths of its output as light and infrared (heat) radiation. NASA Science, Sun Facts: the Sun is constantly sending energy out into space. CAPS p. 27: 'die Son ... gee hitte en lig af'.

items.bewering: Die Aarde kry presies die regte hoeveelheid op sy plek in die Sonnestelsel.
items.blok: Nie te warm en nie te koud nie
items.bron: NASA Science, 'What is the habitable zone or Goldilocks zone?': the habitable zone is 'the area around a star where it is not too hot and not too cold for liquid water to exist', which is a band of distances, not one exact spot. Kopparapu et al. 2013 (Astrophysical Journal, 'Habitable Zones around Main-sequence Stars: New Estimates') put the Sun's conservative habitable zone at about 0.99 to 1.70 AU. NASA StarChild (Jan 2003) and EarthSky: Earth itself is about 147 million km from the Sun in early January and about 152 million km in early July, and the sunlight reaching it is about 7% stronger in January, yet life carries on. The same NASA page says the zone assumes a suitable atmosphere. So there is no single 'exact right amount'. CAPS p. 28 says only 'die regte hoeveelheid', without 'presies'. The fault is the word 'presies': it teaches a knife-edge, so a learner would conclude that Earth moving a little closer or further would end life, and Earth does exactly that every year.
items.regstelling: Drop 'presies' and keep CAPS's own claim: 'Die Aarde kry die regte hoeveelheid op sy plek in die Sonnestelsel.' The following sentences already use 'baie nader' and 'baie verder', which are correctly scoped. Do not add another sentence about orbit distances.

items.bewering: As die Aarde baie nader aan die son was, sou dit hier te warm wees. As die Aarde baie verder weg was, sou dit hier te koud wees. Die Aarde se plek is dus nie te naby nie en nie te ver nie.
items.blok: Nie te warm en nie te koud nie
items.bron: NASA Science, 'What is the habitable zone or Goldilocks zone?': at Mercury's distance Earth's water would boil away; at Pluto's distance its ocean and much of its atmosphere would freeze. 'baie nader' and 'baie verder' are correctly scoped.

items.bewering: Plante, diere en mense kan net lewe waar dit warm genoeg is.
items.blok: Wat lewende dinge by die son kry
items.bron: NASA Science, 'What is the habitable zone?': life as we know it needs liquid water, which needs a temperature that is not too cold. NASA Science, Sun Facts: 'Without the Sun's energy, life as we know it could not exist on our home planet.' 'Warm genoeg' is relative, so polar animals do not contradict it: their environments still allow liquid water and body heat.

items.bewering: Die son se hitte hou die Aarde warm genoeg vir hulle almal.
items.blok: Wat lewende dinge by die son kry
items.bron: NASA Science, Sun Facts (the Sun's energy makes life possible). CAPS p. 28 frames it the same way. Recorded for a person, not as a fault: energyeducation.ca, 'Earth Temperature without GHGs', says that without its greenhouse gases Earth's average would be about -18 °C rather than about +15 °C, so the atmosphere is the Sun's silent partner. The sentence names the Sun as the source of the warmth and does not say 'alone', so it is not false. If the lesson ever adds 'net die son' or similar, it becomes false.

items.bewering: Die son se lig doen nog 'n belangrike werk hier op die Aarde. Plante gebruik daardie lig om self kos te maak.
items.blok: Wat lewende dinge by die son kry
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Photosynthesis': plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to create oxygen and energy in the form of sugar. Kew Endeavour, 'What is photosynthesis' (snippet): plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide and water to make glucose.

items.bewering: Die son se lig en hitte maak al hierdie lewe op die Aarde moontlik.
items.blok: Wat lewende dinge by die son kry
items.bron: NASA Science, Sun Facts: 'Without the Sun's energy, life as we know it could not exist on our home planet.' 'al hierdie lewe' refers back to the plants, animals and people already named, so deep-sea vent life is not claimed.

items.bewering: Sonnestelsel: Die son saam met alles wat om hom beweeg.
items.blok: Sonnestelsel
items.bron: Afrikaanse Wikipedia, 'Sonnestelsel': the Sun and the bodies gravitationally bound to it that orbit it. Read on its own, the entry holds: moons also move around the Sun, together with their planet.

items.blok: planeet
items.bron: IAU Resolution 5A criteria (a)-(c) (Wikipedia, 'IAU definition of planet'): orbits the Sun, nearly round from its own gravity, has cleared the neighbourhood of its orbit. 'op sy eie' excludes moons, matching criterion (d) for dwarf planets. Read alone, the entry holds: Ganymede and Titan are larger than Mercury but do not move on their own, so they are correctly excluded.

items.bewering: wentelbaan: Die pad wat iets in die ruimte oor en oor om 'n ander ding volg.
items.blok: wentelbaan
items.bron: NASA, 'What Is an Orbit?' (nasa.gov grades 5-8; NASA Space Place): 'a regular, repeating path that one object in space takes around another one'. CAPS p. 28 uses 'wentelbaan'.

items.blok: dwergplaneet
items.bron: IAU Resolution 5A: a dwarf planet orbits the Sun, is nearly round, 'has not cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit', and 'is not a satellite' (Wikipedia, 'IAU definition of planet'). NASA Science, Pluto Facts: Pluto shares the Kuiper Belt with similar icy worlds.

opsomming: Een fout om reg te maak: die les sê die Aarde kry 'presies' die regte hoeveelheid lig en hitte, maar die bewoonbare sone is 'n band van afstande, die Aarde se eie afstand van die son wissel elke jaar met sowat 5 miljoen km, en KABV sê net 'die regte hoeveelheid', so skrap 'presies' (alles anders, insluitend die agt planete in volgorde, Pluto se herindeling in 2006, die wentelbaan, die jaar en al vier begrip-inskrywings, is teen bronne bevestig).
